title: Etale local Noetherian model for perfect and relatively flat proper-support data
statement: Work with a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and the canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Derived pullback and tensor are computed with K-flat resolutions with flat terms, and derived direct image with K-injective resolutions. Perfect means etale locally isomorphic in the derived category to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules. Finite presentation of a morphism means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. A module is finitely presented when it locally has a presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. Flatness over a base is flatness of geometric stalks over its corresponding geometric local rings. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; the scheme theoretic support of a finitely presented module is the closed subspace cut out by its annihilator. Let $f:X\to Y$ be of finite presentation, let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be perfect, and let $G^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of quasi-coherent finitely presented modules, termwise flat over $Y$ with termwise support proper over $Y$. There is a jointly surjective family of etale maps $u_a:U_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a\to Y$ with the following data for every $a$. Put $X_a=X\times_YU_a$ and write $v_a:X_a\to X$ for its projection. There are a Noetherian ring $R_{a,0}$ (every ideal is finitely generated), a ring map $R_{a,0}\to R_a$, a finitely presented algebraic space $X_{a,0}$ over $U_{a,0}=\operatorname{Spec}R_{a,0}$, a perfect $E_{a,0}\in D(\mathcal O_{X_{a,0}})$, and a bounded complex $G_{a,0}^\bullet$ of quasi-coherent finitely presented modules, termwise flat over $U_{a,0}$ with termwise support proper over $U_{a,0}$. The space $X_{a,0}$ is locally Noetherian and the terms of $G_{a,0}^\bullet$ are coherent, meaning their modules on affine etale charts are finitely generated over Noetherian rings. There is an isomorphism $X_a\simeq X_{a,0}\times_{U_{a,0}}U_a$ over $U_a$. Writing $p_a:X_a\to X_{a,0}$ for its first projection, there are an isomorphism $Lp_a^*E_{a,0}\simeq Lv_a^*E$ in $D(\mathcal O_{X_a})$ and an isomorphism of cochain complexes $p_a^*G_{a,0}^\bullet\simeq v_a^*G^\bullet$, where both coefficient pullbacks are ordinary termwise tensor pullbacks. The etale restrictions $Lv_a^*E$ are perfect and $v_a^*G^\bullet$ is termwise flat over $U_a$. The models need only be algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and need not carry an $S$-structure.

proof.text: Choose an affine-component etale atlas $\{U_a\to Y\}$ using [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. By base change, $f_a:X_a\to U_a$ is finitely presented and $v_a:X_a\to X$ is etale. The enlarged-site localization description makes restriction by $v_a$ the ordinary exact restriction of structure modules; geometric local rings and module stalks at corresponding geometric points are unchanged by etale restriction. Thus the finite presentations restrict and relative flatness of $G^n$ over $Y$ gives relative flatness of $v_a^*G^n$ over $U_a$. Perfectness also restricts: pull a local bounded finite-free-retract model back to its etale covering of $X_a$. For proper support, a proper closed carrier $Z\hookrightarrow X$ of $G^n$ exists by [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support]. Its base change $Z_a\hookrightarrow X_a$ is proper over $U_a$. The ideal of $Z_a$ kills $v_a^*G^n$, since tensor pullback sends each relation $im=0$ to the same relation. On charts this module is therefore a module over the quotient by that ideal, giving a finite type module on $Z_a$. The reverse carrier implication gives proper scheme-theoretic support on $X_a$. It suffices to construct a model for these restricted data. The argument applies to each $a$ separately.

source.place: Tag 0A1P (lemma-base-change-tensor-perfect), etale affine localization; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0CZI (lemma-module-support-proper-over-base).

proof.text: Fix $a$ and write $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], the spectra $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of finitely generated integer subrings of $R$ have limit $U_a$ and affine transitions. Their index set is small, nonempty and directed: it is a subset of the power set of $R$, contains the image of $\mathbf Z$, and the union of two finite generating sets generates an upper bound. Each $R_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] applied over $\mathbf Z$. Here $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian directly: a nonzero ideal is generated by its least positive element, by division with remainder; the zero ideal has empty generating set.

source.place: Tag 0A1P, paragraph beginning We write R; algebra.tex Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category] to obtain a finitely presented $X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ and $X_a\simeq X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}U_a$. Put $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$ for $i\ge i_0$. These maps are finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], so each $X_i$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source]. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], applied to $T=\lim T_i$ and $W=X_{i_0}$, identifies $X_a$ with $\lim X_i$. The transition maps of the $X_i$ are affine: on any affine scheme test mapping to $X_i$, the transition pullback is the base change of the affine map $T_j\to T_i$, hence affine by the affine-spectrum tensor-product formula. This is precisely an inverse system to which module and perfect continuity apply.

source.place: Tag 0A1P, application of Tag 07SK; spaces-limits.tex Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit).

proof.text: Choose integers $b\le c$ outside which $G^\bullet$ vanishes. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-limit-category] to the finitely many terms in $[b,c]$, choosing a common stage by directedness. For each differential, conjugate it by the chosen term identifications and apply the morphism-descent clause to lift it at a later stage; there are only finitely many, so take one common stage again. The composites $d^{n+1}d^n$ and the zero maps agree after limit pullback. Apply the equality clause to each of these finitely many pairs and pass to a common upper bound. Now $d^{n+1}d^n=0$ at that stage. Put zero terms and zero boundary differentials outside $[b,c]$. This produces a bounded complex $G_i^\bullet$ of finitely presented modules and an isomorphism of cochain complexes with the restricted $G^\bullet$ after ordinary tensor pullback. Finite-presentation modules are quasi-coherent: their local presentations are exactly local cokernel presentations in the definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. All further pullbacks retain the chosen chain isomorphism and the equations because pullback is a functor.

source.place: Tag 0A1P, descent of the bounded complex using Tag 07V7 (lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation); finite number of objects, arrows and equations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-limit-category] to $Lv_a^*E$ on $X_a=\lim X_i$. It descends to a perfect $E_i$ at some later common stage, with a derived isomorphism $Lp_i^*E_i\simeq Lv_a^*E$. Pull the already constructed complex to this stage. Next apply [lem-sfb-space-module-eventually-flat] to each of its finitely many terms, using their relative flatness over $U_a$ established in step 1. Take a common upper bound of the resulting flatness stages. Every term is then flat at this and all later stages. Finally apply [lem-sfb-space-module-eventually-proper-support] successively to those finitely many terms. Earlier proper supports remain proper when moving to a later stage: the carrier equivalence [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support] converts to a proper carrier, [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] preserves properness of that carrier under base change, and the quotient-module construction of step 1 gives a carrier for the tensor-pulled-back module. The carrier equivalence converts back. Module continuity preserves finite presentation, and the eventual-flatness node explicitly gives flatness at every later stage. Perfectness persists by the pullback clause of perfect continuity. Thus one stage has all required flatness and proper-support properties simultaneously. Set $R_{a,0}=R_i$, $X_{a,0}=X_i$, $E_{a,0}=E_i$, $G_{a,0}^\bullet=G_i^\bullet$ there. The two specified comparisons are respectively derived pullback and ordinary termwise tensor pullback, as required.

source.place: Tag 0A1P, successive use of Tags 08K0, 08K2, 09RJ; persistence under further base change.

proof.text: It remains to check local Noetherianity and the stated meaning of coherence. The affine base $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ is locally Noetherian by its one-chart cover [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For any etale scheme chart $V\to X_i$, its composite to $T_i$ is locally of finite presentation by the chart definition for $f_i$, hence locally of finite type. Thus [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $V$ locally Noetherian, proving that $X_i$ is locally Noetherian. Each affine open of $V$ has a Noetherian ring by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. The pullback of each $G_i^n$ to $V$ is finitely presented by module continuity. Under the Zariski/small-etale quasi-coherent equivalence, finite presentation remains finite presentation by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]. On an affine open, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] identifies this with a finitely presented ring module, which is finitely generated by its finite generating presentation. Hence the terms are coherent in exactly the chartwise sense specified in the item. No $S$-structure was descended: all models were constructed over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.
